newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SHARAD YADAV ELECTED JANATA DAL PARTY PRESIDENT

Sharad Yadav has been elected president of the Janata Dal party. He will formally assume charge in two weeks. Sharad Yadav, 52, is a former minister of the union cabinet and one of the key players in implementing the Mandal Commission Report, which recommended affirmative action in government services for the lowest Hindu castes. He is also the party's first elected president since its formation in 1988. The election was marred by litigation and a party split lead by rival candidate Laloo Prasad Yadav.
The Economic Times
PRIVATE PLAYERS TO PROVIDE INTERNET SERVICE

The Telecom Commission has decided to allow private companies to function as Internet service providers. Such providers will not have to pay a licence fee to operate the services for the first two years. The operators will have no gateway for the first two years and will have to route data through the gateway of Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, India's international telecommunications service provider. After two years the Department of Telecommunication may reconsider its decision to exempt the Internet service providers from paying licence fee.
SIEMENS PLANS TO SHED 1,400 EMPLOYEES

Siemens India announced a voluntary retirement scheme for its entire workforce, including senior officers. It hopes to shed 1,400 of its 7,100 workforce in India in the next few months. The voluntary retirement scheme announced by Siemens is a close-ended scheme which can only be availed of until August 31. This deadline was set by the income-tax department, which has granted tax exemption on all payments under the scheme up to a maximum of 500,000 rupees per employee.
COPPER SMELTER PLANT CLOSED AFTER GAS LEAK

A copper smelter plant of Sterlite Industries in Tamil Nadu state was asked to shut down on Sunday after a sulphur dioxide leak that affected about 100 women who were working in a nearby plant. The women developed nausea and were rushed to the Tuticorin hospital. The Tuticorin local administration directed the Sterlite group to shut down the plant as the gas leak has triggered a wave of protest.
Financial Express
GOVERNMENT BANKS PLAN DUAL PRIME LENDING RATES

Government banks will introduce two sets of prime lending rates to protect shrinking spreads following successive rate cuts during the last year. The long term prime lending rate will be slightly higher than the prime lending rate for working capital loans. The State Bank of India has already introduced a higher prime lending rate for project finance. The big government banks cut their prime lending rates by three percentage points between April 1996 and July 1997.
MONEY LAUNDERING BILL TO COVER ECONOMIC OFFENCES

The revenue secretary has said the proposed money-laundering act would cover economic offences in addition to a set of other crimes. He also said the money-laundering bill and the foreign exchange management bill would run parallel. A draft of the money-laundering bill was finalised last week and was submitted to the revenue secretary. The finance secretary chaired a meeting to discuss the foreign exchange management act. It was attended by the representatives of the Reserve Bank.
Business Standard
NEW MODEL TO RAISE PUBLIC FUNDS BY COMPANIES

The corporate sector has worked out a model corporate structure that will permit companies to raise funds from the public without being subject to the regulations applicable to government companies. Under this structure, the promoting company will be an investment company that will raise funds from the public. The money will be invested in a host of group companies which will be the operating companies. The promoting company's equity in the operating companies will be less than 51 percent. The group companies will qualify to be private companies and not to be subsidiaries.
GOVERNMENT FREES 900 BLN WORTH PROJECTS FROM CLEARANCE

The government freed the nine companies it gave autonomy to from seeking the Public Investment Board's clearance for projects worth more than 900 billion rupees. The companies can now go ahead with their projects, to be implemented over the next five years, without waiting for the panel's clearance. The companies which will benefit from this are the Steel Authority of India Ltd, the National Thermal Power Corporation, India's international telecom service provider Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd and Bharat Heavy Electricals. But government oil companies are likely to be hampered by restrictions on investment in joint ventures and subsidiaries.
CAR OUTPUT TO BE INCREASED BY OVER ONE MLN IN TWO YEARS

The domestic car segment has decided to increase production capacity by 1.18 million cars a year in two years. The decision followed a request by the government to assess the projected capacities in the domestic passenger car segment. The 1.18 million projection does not include Maruti Udyog's annual capacity which is projected at a total of 250,000 units. According to the Industry Ministry, South Korea's Daewoo plans to produce 70,000 Cielo cars and 60,000 of its Nubira model. Hyundai Motors plans to produce 100,000 of its Accent cars a year and 250,000 of its small car codenamed HMX.
The Observer
THREE INSTITUTIONS TO RAISE $650 MLN VIA FOREIGN BORROWINGS

The government has given permission to three leading financial institutions to raise $650 million through external commercial borrowings. The Industrial Development Bank got permission for $300 million, the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp for $250 million and the Industrial Finance Corporation for $100 million.
INFLATION DIPS MARGINALLY TO 5.81 PCT

The annual rate of inflation fell by 0.04 percentage points to close the week ended June 21 at 5.81 percent. The fall in inflation based on the wholesale price index came along with a marginal price rise of the commodities under the primary article group. The annual inflation calculated on a point to point basis fell to 5.81 percent in the week ended June 21 from the 5.85 percent a week earlier. The inflation rate during the corresponding week last year was 4.4 percent.
